item.title: Getting Defensive: Week 4 fantasy plays led by Vikings, Seahawks; top streaming defenses
item.description: Gary Davenport breaks down the fantasy football defense landscape headed into Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season.
item.content:encoded:
The rest of the AFC West should be afraid. Terrified. Aghast, even.

Because the Soul Patrol is back, baby!

For those of you who aren’t old and decrepit like this hack, the Soul Patrol was the nickname given to the Jack Tatum-led defenses of the 1970s in Oakland. And three weeks into the 2026 season, no defense in the AFC has more fantasy points than Maxx Crosby and the 3-0 Las Vegas Raiders.

Just one year ago, the Raiders fielded one of the worst defenses in the league. But under first-year head coach Klint Kubiak and defensive coordinator Rob Leonard, the Raiders have been respectable—the Silver and Black ranks 12th in total defense and seventh in scoring defense.

The Raiders have also been racking up big plays—three games in, the Raiders are one of five NFL teams who have double-digit sacks. The Raiders’ nine takeaways lead the league.

Now to be fair, we haven’t exactly seen the Raiders play a Murderer’s Row of opponents—the Los Angeles Chargers, Arizona Cardinals and New Orleans Saints are a combined 2-4. And fantasy managers willing to roll Vegas out this week at home against the red-hot Kansas City Chiefs are straddling the line between brave and insane. And the schedule over the next month is probably going to mean the party’s over.

But it was quite the unexpectedly enjoyable soiree—and with matchup defenses that’s all fantasy managers can ask.

THE NO-DOUBTERS

Minnesota Vikings (vs. Miami Dolphins)

After three weeks, the Minnesota Vikings are the kings of fantasy defenses. The Vikings lead the league in scoring defense at just 12 points per game, have an NFL-high 14 sacks and sit third in the league in takeaways. This week, Brian Flores’ wildly aggressive unit hosts a Miami Dolphins team that could legitimately go 0-17. The Dolphins are tied for last in the league in scoring at a whopping 12 points per game, and Miami’s lone real offensive weapon (running back De’Von Achane) just went down with an ACL tear.

Seattle Seahawks (vs. Los Angeles Chargers)

The Seahawks were the seventh-ranked fantasy defense after two weeks and appeared to have a dream matchup last Sunday with a Washington Commanders team starting their backup quarterback. What happened next was—unexpected. But Seattle was done in in Week 3 more by ill-timed mistakes than a poor defensive outing, and now they return home to face a winless Chargers team that is floundering offensively. Take a breath—an angry Seattle defense is going to take your frustration out on the Bolts along with their own.

Pittsburgh Steelers (at Cleveland Browns)

The Steelers started the season hot defensively—T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith got after the quarterback, the Steelers piled up big plays and the fantasy points followed. Things cooled last week against Joe Burrow and the Bengals, but look for the Steelers to get back on track Thursday night in Cleveland. The Browns may be 2-1, but the team has been inconsistent offensively, Deshaun Watson has been dropped nine times in three games, and the Browns have been a top-10 fantasy matchup for opposing defenses dating back to 2025.

Cleveland Browns (vs. Pittsburgh Steelers)

Fun fact—the Cleveland Browns have lost just one of their last eight home games against the Steelers. Fun fact No. 2—the Steelers have been a favorable fantasy matchup for defenses so far this season, surrendering the fifth-most fantasy points per game to the position. The Browns aren’t quite as good defensively as they were a year ago, but the team has rebounded nicely after a miserable Week 1 in Jacksonville. Points are going to be at a premium on Thursday night.

Kansas City Chiefs (at Las Vegas Raiders)

This one’s dicey enough that it maybe should be a streamer more than a sure thing (Word salad alert!). But the Chiefs have played excellent defense in two of their three games, and Steve Spagnuolo is one of the best defensive coordinators in the league. This is going to be the stiffest test the 3-0 Raiders have faced and then some. If the Raiders’ struggles in the run game continue (just 100 yards a game) and Kirk Cousins has to try to outduel Patrick Mahomes, Spags will heat Cousins up. Cousins is many things. Mobile is not one of them.

STREAMERS OF THE WORLD, UNITE!

Baltimore Ravens (vs. Tennessee Titans)

The Baltimore defense was supposed to be much-improved in 2026. The Ravens may be 2-1, but it’s more in spite of that defense than because of it—Baltimore is allowing almost 31 points and 400 yards of offense per game. Of course, that came against actual NFL offenses, and the Tennessee Titans qualify as one in name only. No team in the AFC has gained fewer yards per game this season. Only two teams are averaging fewer points per game. If ever there was a “get right” spot, this is it.

Buffalo Bills (vs. New England Patriots)

To be clear, while the Bills may be 3-0, Buffalo’s defense has not played especially well in many respects this year—the Bills are 24th in the league in total defense and have allowed 26 points per game. But the New England Patriots are a dysfunctional mess on offense. The offensive line is getting pushed around. The receivers can’t get open. And quarterback Drake Maye is a turnover machine dating back to last year’s postseason. The Patriots are fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to defenses this year.

Chicago Bears (vs. New York Jets)

The fantasy production of the Chicago defense has quietly been improving—a unit that didn’t look great in Week 1 at Carolina just positively put the clamps on an undefeated Philadelphia Eagles team at Soldier Field Monday night. The Jets have looked improved offensively with Geno Smith at quarterback, but last week’s numbers were inflated by Detroit’s decision that playing defense is stupid. The Bears are a top-10 fantasy defense for the season—and a top-10 fantasy defense in Week 4.

Green Bay Packers (at Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

It might seem strange to see the Packers listed here. After all, the last time we saw the Pack, they were giving up all the rushing yards ever to the Atlanta Falcons. The Packers had an OK fantasy outing in Week 2 against the Jets, but that was sandwiched inside two clunkers. But this week the Packers head south to take on a Buccaneers team that was one of the best fantasy matchups for defenses this season before Baker Mayfield got hurt. Now, Tampa will likely be rolling out an undrafted rookie under center.

New Orleans Saints (vs. Atlanta Falcons)

Feeling froggy in Week 4? Playing in a league with a bunch of defense-hoarding jerkfaces? Well, if you’re at the end of your rope, the Saints are the defense for you. New Orleans hasn’t played very well defensively this year, and the Falcons may have found a winning formula last week—play football like it’s 1956. But this is also a Saints team that beat the Ravens in Baltimore two weeks ago facing a Falcons team that has given up the second-most fantasy points to defenses in 2026.

CAVEAT EMPTOR, FOLKS

Denver Broncos (at San Francisco 49ers)

Despite an absolutely brutal schedule out of the gate (at Kansas City and home against the Jaguars and Rams) the Denver defense is back in the top 10 in fantasy points—the Broncos shook off a disastrous opener at Arrowhead to shut down two potent offenses in the second half. Were this game at Mile High, this writer might just go ahead and roll Denver out. But it’s in Santa Clara against a 49ers offense that has scored 98 points in three games despite numerous injuries on offense.

Jacksonville Jaguars (at Cincinnati Bengals)

After something of a letdown game on the road in Denver in Week 2, the Jaguars posted their second dominant defensive performance in three weeks against the Patriots Sunday, logging three sacks and three takeaways while allowing just six points. But for whatever reason, the Jaguars just aren’t the same team away from EverBank Stadium, and last week the Cincinnati offense handed Pittsburgh’s defense their worst fantasy effort of the season. Not saying to drop the Jags necessarily. But if you start them, temper expectations.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather.

item.title: Fantasy Football Backup RB Rankings: Injuries are thrusting second options into prominent roles for Week 4
item.description: Here are Fred Zinkie's top backup RBs to note for fantasy football in Week 4.
item.content:encoded:
This list has undergone a major shakeup this week, as injuries to three starting running backs (De'Von Achane, Travis Etienne Jr. and Breece Hall) have provided fantasy managers with fresh options. That news couldn't come at a better time, as some of the RBs who were expected to contribute to a shared backfield, such as Rico Dowdle and Kenny Gainwell, have been major disappointments thus far.

Fantasy managers should base their upcoming roster moves on team needs. Some managers are sitting at 1-2 or 0-3 and need someone who can get them a win this week. In that case, Braelon Allen is the top option. Other managers may need RB depth in the form of someone who will have a significant role in their team's offense for the remainder of the season, which perfectly describes Ollie Gordon II. Finally, the managers who are strong at the RB position and can afford to stash someone who may eventually become a league-winning player can opt for the likes of Kyle Monangai or Rachaad White.

Ollie Gordon II, Dolphins (5% rostered on Yahoo)

Gordon will enjoy one week atop this list before likely graduating to starter status after Week 4. The physical runner, who once logged a 1,732-yard, 21-TD season at Oklahoma State, is set to take over for Achane, who will miss the remainder of the season due to a torn ACL.

The scouting report on Gordon is that, while he isn't a complete zero as a receiver, his skills lie primarily in his ability to wear down defenses with his hard running style. And given that Malik Willis is most likely to scramble when under pressure, we should expect Gordon to get few fantasy points through the air. Gordon will also be hampered by his membership in a Miami offense that ranks last in points scored. That being said, running backs who could be permanent starters are rarely available on the waiver wire, which makes Gordon a must-add player for anyone who needs help at the position.

Finally, it's worth noting that Jaylen Wright, who missed Week 3 with a foot injury, could factor into the Dolphins backfield as well. Both players should be added in standard formats.

Braelon Allen, Jets, (20%)

Although Breece Hall seems to have escaped a major injury, his quad ailment will likely keep him out of Week 4. That's great news for Allen, who is the only other Jets RB who has touched the ball this season. The problem is that Allen hasn't done much with his opportunities, averaging 3.2 yards per carry and 2.8 yards per reception.

Although Isaiah Davis will likely get some opportunities, Allen is the favorite for early-down and goal-line work. Fantasy managers should keep their expectations in check, but Allen is a worthwhile option for those who need to replace Hall this week, especially given the Jets will face a mediocre Bears run defense.

Kyle Monangai, Bears (83%)

After impressive performances during the initial two weeks, Monangai laid an egg in a lopsided Week 3 win over the Eagles. The hard-charging runner played just 22 snaps, in comparison to 50 snaps for D'Andre Swift. And he was much less impressive than Swift when given opportunities, gaining 31 yards on 10 carries.

Despite the lackluster effort, Monangai is a big part of the Bears offense. Swift got off to a great start on Monday Night Football, and head coach Ben Johnson decided to run with the hot hand. The expectation here is for Monangai to have larger roles in future weeks. The good news for both players is that the Bears lead the NFL with 553 rushing yards.

TreVeyon Henderson, Patriots (94%)

The Patriots struggled to run the ball against a stout Jaguars defense, which was a big reason for a blowout loss. Rhamdondre Stevenson and Henderson had 10 and nine touches, respectively, and both players did little with their opportunities. After a strong Week 2 performance, Henderson has achieved a relatively even split, with Stevenson remaining more involved in the passing game.

The concern for both players is that the Patriots offense hasn't looked nearly as good as it did last season, particularly QB Drake Maye. Henderson should get 10 touches in a huge Week 4 game in Buffalo before the team enjoys an easier stretch of games beginning in Week 5. But with little pass-catching work, he's a boom-or-bust flex option who needs to score a touchdown to exceed expectations.

Rachaad White, Commanders (58%)

White could be on the verge of getting more touches. After outplaying Jacory Croskey-Merritt in Week 2, he gained 35 yards on eight carries last week against the Seahawks in comparison to 36 yards on 19 carries by JCM. White, who dealt with a shoulder injury at times during the game, was not especially involved in the passing game, but he managed to get into the end zone on his only catch.

Given that they are coming off an impressive win over the Seahawks, the Commanders are unlikely to immediately mess with their backfield plan. Croskey-Merritt will continue to grind out difficult yards while White will get some high-impact touches. But White could soon earn more carries, and the Commanders have two decent home matchups (Colts, Giants) in the next two weeks.

RJ Harvey, Broncos (78%)

With rookie Jonah Coleman on the sidelines, the Broncos deployed Harvey and starter J.K. Dobbins in specific roles during a Week 3 win over the Rams. Dobbins tallied 17 carries and one catch, while Harvey carried the ball just twice but led the team with six receptions. Harvey was much more effective than Dobbins, who averaged just 2.9 yards per carry.

Coleman is on IR, which simplifies this backfield for the coming weeks. Harvey will be much more valuable in PPR formats, where he is a viable flex option. He could also earn more rushing work, since Dobbins has averaged just 3.5 yards per carry.

Keaton Mitchell, Chargers (32%)

The winless Chargers are re-evaluating everything, and running back Omarion Hampton's role is no longer safe. The second-year pro looked sluggish once again last Sunday, while Mitchell averaged 6.5 yards on eight carries and took one of his three catches into the end zone.

Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was hyping up Mitchell during the offseason, and he should continue to give his speediest running back more opportunities to jumpstart this offense. And while Mitchell lacks the size for a heavy role, his career average of 6.2 yards per carry shows that he doesn't need many touches to rack up plenty of yards. Although it's hard to envision the coaching staff straying too far from Hampton, who was a first-round pick in 2025, Mitchell could rise up this list in a hurry with an electrifying Week 4 performance in a virtual must-win game at the Seahawks.

Alvin Kamara, Saints (43%)

We have seen Aaron Jones Sr. turn back the clock the past two weeks and handle a heavy workload in a Vikings backfield that is missing Jordan Mason. Can Kamara do the same thing, now that the Saints are going to play multiple games without Etienne? Probably not, but that doesn't mean that he can't be a flex option.

Kamara gained 36 yards on nine carries and caught one pass in a Week 3 loss to the Raiders, and is now set to share backfield opportunities with Kendre Miller for the foreseeable future. The veteran is not the player he used to be, but he likely still has a knack at the goal line and in the passing game, which could result in some weeks with double-digit fantasy points. And it's worth noting that Miller, who has long struggled to win over multiple coaching staffs, fumbled last week.

Woody Marks, Texans (52%)

A Houston offense that didn't run the ball well last season hasn't looked much better this year. Their struggles continued in a Week 3 loss to the Colts, with Marks and David Montgomery each averaging 3.0 yards per carry. Both backs had minimal participation in the passing game as well. Marks does deserve credit for tallying a 1-yard rushing score.

Marks continues to have some involvement in each game, and it was great to see him used near the end zone. He has decent odds of getting 7-10 points in PPR leagues each week, which will make him a low-end flex play when we reach the bye weeks.

Blake Corum, Rams (87%)

Through two games, Corum and Kyren Williams had similar touch totals, despite Williams enjoying a much larger snap share. But things swung wildly in Williams' favor during a narrow Week 3 loss to the Broncos, with the veteran logging 15 carries and seven catches. Corum was mostly an afterthought, tallying just 15 total yards on six carries and two receptions.

Despite the lopsided one-week split, Corum is still an integral part of the Rams offense. But like Henderson, his lack of work in the passing game means that he will have a single-digit fantasy total unless he crosses the goal line. And with Williams coming off his best game of the season, Corum needs to make a statement in Week 4.

The best of the rest, factoring in current Flex value and long-term potential.

  • Emanuel Wilson, Seahawks

  • Tyjae Spears, Titans

  • Jaylen Wright, Dolphins

  • Kaleb Johnson, Packers

  • Rico Dowdle, Steelers

  • Kendre Miller, Saints

  • Tyler Allgeier, Cardinals

  • Mike Washington Jr., Raiders

  • Brian Robinson Jr., Falcons

  • Isaiah Davis, Jets

  • Kaelon Black, 49ers

  • Kenny Gainwell, Buccaneers

  • Tank Bigsby, Eagles

  • Emmett Johnson, Chiefs

  • Chris Rodriguez Jr., Jaguars

  • Justice Hill, Ravens

Injured backups to stash

  • Jordan Mason, Vikings

  • Jonah Coleman, Broncos

  • Zach Charbonnet, Seahawks

  • Jonathon Brooks, Panthers

item.title: Cowboys rookie report: Jaishawn Barham delivers big in Ravens loss
item.description: Jaishawn Barham was so good last week.
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys’ trip to Brazil ended in frustration, with the Baltimore Ravens winning on a last-second field goal. For the rookie class, there were reasons for encouragement. Caleb Downs helped create an early scoring opportunity, while Jaishawn Barham produced two second-half stops that gave Dallas a chance to take control. The challenge remains turning those individual moments into a complete defensive performance.

But here is how each rookie fared this week, listed in draft order, and any undrafted players worth noting after that. 

Caleb Downs

(Defensive snaps: 64 | Tackles: 3 | TFL: 0 | Sacks: 0 | INT: 0 | Passes defended: 0)

Downs’ biggest contribution came early, stopping Derrick Henry for no gain on fourth-and-one and handing Dallas possession at Baltimore’s 30-yard line. That short field became an important Cowboys touchdown which added weight to Down’s stop. His tackle total was modest, but the importance of that stop was considerable. This was a game with a valuable individual highlight, alongside a couple of things to clean up.

Malachi Lawrence

(Defensive snaps: 17 | Tackles: 2 | TFL: 0 | Sacks: 0 | Passes defended: 0 | Pressures: 0 | Special-teams tackles: 1)

Lawrence assisted on two defensive tackles and contributed a kickoff tackle, but his opportunities to rush Lamar Jackson were limited. He made only three pass-rush snaps, with no pressure generated. That small sample matters when judging the performance as Dallas needs more disruption from its edge defenders, but Lawrence had relatively few chances to provide it. His contribution was mainly supporting the run defense and covering kicks. 

Jaishawn Barham

(Defensive snaps: 50 | Tackles: 7 | TFL: 2 | Sacks: 0 | INT: 0 | Passes defended: 0 | Pressures: 1)

Barham provided the strongest rookie performance, particularly when Dallas desperately needed a response. His fourth-and-goal stop against Henry denied Baltimore a touchdown, and another tackle behind the line on the following Ravens possession helped keep the Cowboys in the fight. Those were substantial plays against one of the league’s most difficult runners to bring down. Brian Schottenheimer also praised his command of the defense while handling the green-dot communication duties. 

There were mistakes alongside the highlights. Barham did make two missed tackles against the run and four completions for 50 yards in coverage. His response was the encouraging part. He continued making decisive plays rather than allowing the difficult moments to define his night. 

LT Overton

(Defensive snaps: 15 | Tackles: 2 | TFL: 0 | Sacks: 0 | INT: 0 | Passes defended: 0 | Pressures: 0)

Overton’s limited appearance earned an encouraging initial PFF grade of 77.4. His contribution came against the run, but he generated no pressures on six pass-rush snaps. It was a promising small sample, with pass-rush production still to develop.

item.title: Jerry Jones: No explanation for end of Ravens loss that you're satisfied with
item.description: The Cowboys' chances of winning Sunday's game against the Ravens in Brazil unraveled in the final seconds of the fourth quarter.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys' chances of winning Sunday's game against the Ravens in Brazil unraveled in the final seconds of the fourth quarter.

After the team used its final timeout after a short run by quarterback Dak Prescott on second down from the 5-yard-line, they dialed up a pass play that appeared to get wide receiver George Pickens open in the end zone. Prescott threw the ball away as Pickens got free, which both he and head coach Brian Schottenheimer said was by design after the game.

During a Tuesday appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was asked about the sequence from the timing of the timeout through Prescott's throw.

“There’s no explanation that you’re satisfied with," Jones said. "None. Let’s be sure that we all understand that. They don't have one that they’re satisfied with. We made mistakes during that time, there’s no question about it. There’s no explanation. There’s an evaluation of how to not make the same mistakes again, which is what you should be doing. We can’t get that back. No way to get it back. What you can do is use it — if there’s any aspect of it that you want to just not even think happened. Any aspect of it, use it to get better.”

The Cowboys settled for a field goal with seven seconds left, which turned out to be just enough time for the Ravens to set up a 56-yard game-winning field goal of their own. The handling of the kickoff, which went for a touchback that took no time off the clock, was another matter lacking a satisfying rationale that might make the loss sit better with anyone.

item.title: Lions vs. Jets Song of the Game: ‘Dashboard’ by Modest Mouse
item.description: “Oh it would've been, could've been worse than you would ever know”
item.content:encoded:
After a brief hiatus, “Song of the Game” has returned, back by popular demand of our Editor in Chief and Sticktator, Jeremy Reisman. While I’ve been absolutely swamped between work, writing/editing, podcasting, being a husband and a parent, the next half hour I’ll spend writing this is a welcome break of such serious bellyaching about the secondary.

Lions vs. Jets Week 3 Song of the Game: “Dashboard” by Modest Mouse

Growing up in the day and age of burning CDs to create the soundtrack of your bus rides to and from school, Modest Mouse was a staple of my collection. “Float On” and “Ocean Breathes Salty” spun a bunch on my Sony D-EJ360 Walkman. It hit me right in the midst of my percolating angst as middle school tested my place in the world, and Modest Mouse was just what the doctor ordered.

“Dashboard” is the lead single from the band’s fifth studio album—a track guitarist and songwriter Johnny Marr, formerly of The Smiths, worked on during his first day riffing with Modest Mouse. It’s much more dance-driven pop rock than the slacker rock the band debuted with a decade prior, but even in a different flavor, it’s still damn good.

Modest Mouse’s lineup has changed a bunch over the band’s life cycle, as has the Detroit Lions coaching staff over Dan Campbell’s six years as head coach. Aaron Glenn was one of my favorite hires Campbell made at the start of his tenure, and what he managed to accomplish as a defensive coordinator in 2024 was nothing short of remarkable. It led him to taking a head coaching position with the New York Jets the year after, and while it was a rocky start for the former Jets cornerback, he’s undoubtedly got that team in a position that feels eerily similar to the way Campbell had the Lions in 2022. They’re still feeling out the way to win, but they’re right there—and with tons of draft capital in this upcoming draft.

Oh, it should’ve been, could’ve been worse than you would ever know
Well, you told me about nowhere well it sounds like someplace I’d like to go

Detroit’s defense is still very much a work in progress, especially on the backend, and that’s not something you want to hear about a football team through three weeks of regular season play. Many drew tired of Glenn’s unwillingness to spy mobile quarterbacks, and found him to be overaggressive by the end of his time in Detroit, and we’re seeing how any place other than where we’re at with this defense is someplace we’d like to see it go.

Well, it would’ve been, could’ve been worse than you would ever know
Oh, the dashboard melted, but we still have the radio

And yet, with as bad as the defense has been—with the dashboard melted—we still have the Lions offense playing their same ol’ tunes. 31 points in three straight games, and this game would’ve been, could’ve been worse than you would ever know had it not been for this offense keeping this team in the win column.

Well we scheme and we scheme but we always blow it

We spent all week waiting to see the adjustments Kelvin Sheppard and the defense would make after getting embarrassed on “Thursday Night Football.” What sort of adjustments could they possibly make to clean up that mess? But up until the fourth quarter, the Lions held the Jets to just 10 points. Detroit had a comfortable 24-10 lead, they had schemed and schemed… but they ended up blowing that lead, letting the Jets tie the game with a little over four minutes remaining in the game.

We’ve yet to crash, but we still might as well enjoy it
Standing at a light switch to each east and west horizon
Every dawn you’re surprising
And in the evening one’s consoling
Saying, “See it wasn’t quite as bad as.”

Four plays later, the Lions have the lead, the defense forces a game-winning turnover, and I spent my op-ed this week reminding everyone that while the Lions’ dashboard is melted, we’ve yet to crash, and the radio’s still working, so we might as well enjoy it.

If you want to relive previous Lions seasons, you can find the playlists we curated below: 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022. And if you want to read previous versions of our Song of the Game columns, you can find those here.

item.title: Andy Reid: I'll let you know when Josh Simmons is coming back
item.description: The Chiefs have started the season 3-0 despite not having their starting left tackle available.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs have started the season 3-0 despite not having their starting left tackle available.

Josh Simmons has been sidelined by a back injury that’s been considered week-to-week. But it’s currently unclear if Simmons will return to practice in advance of Sunday’s matchup with the 3-0 Raiders.

“I'll tell you what, I will let you guys know when Josh is coming back. I'll be the first to tell you,” head coach Andy Reid said in his Monday news conference. “We’ll just see how all that works.”

Simmons appeared in eight games as a rookie in 2025.

Undrafted rookie Khalil Benson has started in Simmons’ stead at left tackle and has helped keep Patrick Mahomes upright. The quarterback has been sacked just four times through the first three weeks.

item.title: Browns need to ‘spread the help’ versus the Steelers in Week 4
item.description: The Cleveland Browns offense has some holes at times, including not giving enough help to rookie LT Spencer Fano
item.content:encoded:
The Cleveland Browns are 2-1 heading into a big Thursday Night Football matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers, where the home team is the underdog. Despite the Browns strong start and playoff contention early in the season, Cleveland’s offensive line has not performed well. Whether it is PFF grades, earning Frownies, or just the overall film, very few are lauding the unit upfront.

The line was also not one of the reasons mentioned by fans for why the team is 2-1:

The line’s concerns only grow if center Elgton Jenkins cannot play on Thursday.

This offseason, OL Spencer Fano was considered the capstone of the new and improved Browns offensive line. The first offensive lineman selected in the 2026 NFL draft, Fano has not played poorly but, as noted in takeaways from Week 3, Cleveland’s offense has done him no favors:

Rookie Spencer Fano put on an island; looked like a rookie much of the game. Cleveland’s offense didn’t give him a lot of help and expected him to hold up. Unfortunately, it looks like film from the first two games showed that Fano could be beaten inside because Carolina attacked him there a lot.

This analysis was backed up by former Browns and Ohio State Buckeyes star LeCharles Bentley a day later:

I wish the Browns spread the help in pass protection a bit better. It’s a tall ask for a rookie left tackle to be on an island.

In his Substack article, Bentley showed a video where Cleveland slid protection to the right, with five blockers for just three Panthers defenders. That not only left Fano blocking one-on-one, but also gave his defender a much larger area for his defender to attack. Instead of having a left guard and another defender directly to Fano’s right, Zion Johnson is blocking no one between the center and right guard:

This is not a mistake by Johnson; instead, it was the protection call by the offense.

Against an aggressive, veteran, and versatile Steelers defense, the Browns need to heed Bentley’s desire to “spread the help in pass protection” in Week 4. Otherwise, Deshaun Watson may not have a chance to get the offense going.

How do you feel like Fano has played so far as a rookie? Do you think Monken will make some protection adjustmenets for the Steelers?

item.content:encoded:
Welcome to the third edition of the Weekly Stat Review! A frustrating 3 point loss has the Carolina Panthers falling behind in the most important stat of them all – wins.

If you had the displeasure of watching the whole game, you can guess the direction the stats this series is concerned with have taken. Just for fun, let’s take a look at where things stand anyway.

Offense

Explosive Play Rate

Percentage of plays that qualify as an explosive play. Explosive plays being a carry of 10 or more yards or a pass attempt gaining 20 or more yards.

Week 3 @ CLE: 9.5%

2026 average: 10.8% (8th in NFL)

2025: 8.8% (23rd in NFL)

Pressure Rate Allowed

Percentage of dropbacks with a pressure or sack allowed.

Week 3 @ CLE: 16%

2026 average: League ranking will be updated when available.

2025: 30.9%

3rd Down Conversion Rate

Rate of 3rd downs that converted to 1st downs.

Week 3 @ CLE: 26.7%

2026 average: 36.8% (23rd in NFL)

2025: 36.5% (25th in NFL)

Defense

Zone Coverage Rate

Percentage of coverage snaps spent in a zone defense. Only yearly average will be noted each week going forward.

2026 average: 80% (13th in NFL)

2025: 78% zone coverage

Pressure Rate

Percentage of pass rush opportunities that resulted in a sack or pressure.

Week 3 @ CLE: 15.4%

2026 average: 15.0% (19th in NFL)

2025: 10.1% (31st in NFL)

3rd Down Stop Rate

Rate of 3rd downs allowed to be converted into 1st downs.

Week 3 @ CLE: 33.3%

2026 average: 45.2% (23rd in NFL)

2025: 48.1% (32nd in NFL)

BONUS Stat of the Week

The Panthers are averaging 9 penalties called against them per game, which is the 4th highest rate in the NFL. The two teams the Panthers have lost against so far, the Chicago Bears and Cleveland Browns, hold the 2nd and 3 highest rates in the league. In other words, the Panthers have played in some ugly football games so far that have been heavily influenced by the yellow flags flying onto the field.

item.title: AP NFL Power Rankings Week 4: Jaguars crash Top 5
item.description: The Arrowhead Pride team ranks the league from top to bottom.
item.content:encoded:
New challenge unlocked for quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs: drive down the field for a game-winning field goal in seven seconds or less, as the Baltimore Ravens accomplished on Sunday in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, against the Dallas Cowboys.

The Brazil tilt was the first game in NFL history in which both teams scored in the final 10 seconds of a regular-season game. It headlined another wild week of NFL action, which whittled the remaining unbeaten down to only five.

And they were all who we expected, right?

Among the 3-0 unbeatens are the Chiefs, Buffalo Bills and San Francisco 49ers —solid franchises of the past decade. Joining the unbeaten club are two of the more surprising teams (represented in our power rankings as such, as they have shot up the rankings)— the Las Vegas Raiders and Minnesota Vikings.

I think I speak for all of Chiefs Kingdom when I say it’s fun to look forward to a Chiefs-Raiders matchup again, as they’ll clash in Week 4. The rivalry is more fun when there are stakes and both teams are competitive.

But let’s not get too far ahead of ourselves. Let’s see how the AP power rankings shook out this week.

Biggest risers:Pittsburgh Steelers,Jacksonville Jaguars, and Cleveland Browns +7

Biggest fallers:New England Patriots and Green Bay Packers -8

This week, along with myself, staff voters were: Caleb James, Ron Kopp Jr., Rocky Magana, and Jared Sapp.

1. San Francisco 49ers (3rd)

I’m going to take the low-hanging fruit here. Brock Purdy has looked purdy nice to start this season. He currently holds the second-highest MVP odds.

2. Buffalo Bills (2nd)

Five turnovers and still coming away with the win is tough to do.

3. Kansas City Chiefs (4th)

I give myself headaches trying to do the mental gymnastics of the haters who believe the conspiracy theories of the refs favoring the Chiefs.

4. Jacksonville Jaguars (11th)

In true Jaguars fashion, they aren’t getting the respect they probably deserve. The top two storylines I saw coming out of this one? Josh Hines-Allen fighting a ball boy for Travis Hunter’s first career interception ball. And Trevor Lawrence oddly kneeling down at the 1-yard line instead of scoring a touchdown with eight minutes left.

5. Seattle Seahawks (1st)

The return of quarterback Sam Darnold did not spell victory for the ‘Hawks. They suffered their first loss since November 2025.

6. Baltimore Ravens (7th)

The flight from Rio back to Baltimore was about 10 hours. The Ravens took possession with seven seconds left in the fourth quarter to win. This means Ravens’ players could have watched their game-winning drive 5,142 times on the flight home.

7. Cincinnati Bengals (5th)

The quarterback who supposedly has ice running through his veins falls up short in the 4th quarter—once again. Burrow sure gains a lot of national respect from that Super Bowl loss, checks notes, five years ago.

8. Philadelphia Eagles (6th)

This team reminds me of the 2025 Kansas City Chiefs. A team that looks tired, bored, and like the league has figured them out. They need some sort of shakeup.

9. Minnesota Vikings (9th)

A 3-0 start, and they shipped quarterback JJ McCarthy to New York for draft capital. The McCarthy selection will go down as one of the biggest blunders in their franchise history.

10. Los Angeles Rams (8th)

I’d be livid as a Rams fan over that pass interference call that negated a game-sealing interception in the fourth quarter. But also, maybe don’t give a 16-point halftime lead or throw a pick-six to put you in that do-or-die spot?

11. Chicago Bears (10th)

Although Caleb Williams was on the sideline in a hoodie, the Bears still looked like one of the top teams in the NFC with journeyman Case Keenum.

12. Las Vegas Raiders (18th)

Alright, respect where it’s due. The Raiders have looked solid to start the year and have already matched their 2025 win total. 

But enough of that….IT’S RAIIIIIDERS WEEK.

13. Detroit Lions (14th)

Jahmyr Gibbs is an absolute cheat code on the football field.

14. Denver Broncos (13th)

How long can this team survive by winning bizarre games with absurd fourth-quarter comebacks?

15. Dallas Cowboys (16th)

Such an insane and hilarious way for the Cowboys to lose a football game.

16. Pittsburgh Steelers (23rd)

Credit where credit is due. Pittsburgh delivered a solid divisional win. Now they must repeat on a short week against Cleveland.

17. Indianapolis Colts (22nd)

The Colts achieved their first win on American soil in almost a full calendar year!

18. New Orleans Saints (17th)

Tyler Shough impresses even in the loss. The Saints could really go on a run and surprise some folks. Their next six opponents are the Falcons, Vikings, Giants, Steelers, Browns, and Panthers. A fairly favorable schedule.

19. New York Giants (21st)

If your starting quarterback goes down, it’s favorable to have the Tennessee Titans on your schedule the following week.

20. New England Patriots (12th)

What is wrong with Drake Maye? Talk about regression.

21. Arizona Cardinals (24th)

What would you give up for the Chiefs to acquire Marvin Harrison Jr.?

22. Cleveland Browns (29th)

Browns fans really are an unlucky bunch. They’re upset if they lose, yet upset if they win because they hate their current quarterback.

23. Green Bay Packers (15th)

Dreadful performance in front of the home crowd at Lambeau. Does head coach Matt LaFleur make it through the season?

24. Houston Texans (19th)

This has to be one of the least-talked-about teams in the NFL. On paper, one of the league’s top defenses. But for the second season in a row, they’re 0-3.

25. Atlanta Falcons (31st)

An offensive explosion at Lambeau has reignited faint hope in Atlanta. When Bijan Robinson and Drake London are both hot, and they get competent quarterback play, this offense will be tough to slow down.

26. Carolina Panthers (20th)

Honestly, I was shocked to find out the Panthers will be gracing our television screens in primetime next week.

27. Washington Commanders (28th)

The team is the lowest in our power rankings and is coming off the most solid win in Week 3. But there isn’t much to be excited about with this team.

28. Los Angeles Chargers (25th)

Chiefs fans honestly couldn’t lose with the matchup on Sunday. Either the Bills were embarrassed at home by the 0-2 Chargers or the AFC West offseason champs fell to 0-3. I’ll take this result.

29. New York Jets (27th)

The Jets honestly look to be improved this season. But from the outset, it is obvious they are already looking forward to 2027.

30. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (26th)

Baker joins the list of starting quarterbacks to miss time this season. What a brutal season for the Bucs, and one has to wonder how long head coach Todd Bowles has a job.

31. Miami Dolphins (32nd)

With Devon Achane going down for the season, 0-17 may legitimately be in the cards.

32. Tennessee Titans (30th)

This season will produce the most depressing country songs ever written in Nashville.

item.title: The Raiders are done being punchlines
item.description: The Raiders are winning games, and it isn’t a fluke.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL regular season is a race — one that the Las Vegas Raiders have struggled to run for the better part of a decade.

It’s not for lack of trying, though. Since 2020, the Raiders have had six head coaches of all types. They brought Jon Gruden out of the Monday Night Football booth back in 2018. When he resigned in controversial fashion, special teams coordinator Rich Bisaccia took over and helped lead the Raiders to the playoffs. Despite that, Bisaccia wasn’t promoted from interim head coach to full-time head coach. That title, instead, went to Josh McDaniels, which ended the exact same way his tenure in Denver did a decade earlier – with a one-way flight back to Foxborough after a 9-16 record. This time around, the Raiders did promote the interim head coach as Antonio Pierce was given the job ahead of the 2024 season and was one-and-done after a 4-13 season.

And after years of retreads, quote unquote “gurus,” and a player’s coach who was given a job he was vastly under qualified for, the Raiders were supposed to snap out of their funk in 2025 when they hired Super Bowl champion and future Hall of Famer Pete Carroll, who then traded for quarterback Geno Smith, of whom he had shared much success with in Seattle. And somehow, Carroll was the biggest disaster of them all, going 2-15 and becoming the second straight one-and-done head coach in Vegas.

But this time is different. Truly. After one of the more disappointing seasons in team history, the Raiders braintrust went back to the Seahawks well and hired Klint Kubiak, the offensive coordinator who was fresh off helping Sam Darnold and Seattle win the Super Bowl. Due to recent history, though, as well as a perceived lack of talent, expectations were understandably low for Vegas – and that seems to be perfectly okay with them.

After winning just two games in 2025, the Raiders have three wins before the end of September and are one of just five teams that remain unbeaten heading into Week 4. Not only are they winning games, they are doing so convincingly. They defeated the Miami Dolphins 27-13 to kickoff the season. And sure, the Dolphins aren’t a good team. However, had Vegas barely eked out a win or lost, we would have crucified them, so they deserve credit for winning decisively. In Week 2, they went on the road and beat a Chargers team who was a popular pick to win the AFC West by the score of 26-14 and picked off Justin Herbert twice. In Week 3, against a fellow on-the-rise team in the New Orleans Saints, Vegas outlasted New Orleans to win a 35-27, with Maxx Crosby forcing a fumble late to help secure the win for the Raiders. The win marks their first 3-0 start since 2021, and just their third such start since the turn of the century.

It’s not just that the Raiders are winning, it’s that these aren’t flukes. These aren’t stolen wins like Week 2 in 2024 where the Ravens blow a 23-13 fourth-quarter lead to Gardner Minshew. Nor is it a Christmas Day win over the Chiefs despite only gaining 205 yards of total offense. The 2026 Raiders through three weeks currently rank eighth in pass success rate, and Kirk Cousins leads the NFL in touchdown passes while ranking 10th in EPA per pass, per Sumer Sports. Not only are the Raiders efficient offensively, but Rob Leonard’s defense has been superb. Las Vegas currently has the third best defensive EPA per play, trailing only the Seattle Seahawks and the Minnesota Vikings. Their four interceptions lead the NFL, and their 10 sacks rank fourth. None of this is accidental. This team isn’t a mockery masking as a menace. The 2026 Raiders are kicking doors down, not sneaking in the back when no one his looking.

Does this mean they will be one of the final 14 teams playing in January? That’s not necessarily the point. The point is that they’re in the race – something we haven’t been able to say in a very long time.

That’s the cold open – this is the Hot Read.

Three and out

Respect Brock Purdy

I’m mostly saying this to myself. Back in the summer, I released my top 40 NFL quarterbacks ranking, where I slotted Purdy in at No. 18 – one spot ahead of Aaron Rodgers and one spot below C.J. Stroud. Allow me to omit my wrongdoing and tell you all how fantastic Purdy has played thus far.

Through three games, Purdy is lapping every other quarterback in total EPA. He currently sits with an EPA mark of 56.42 – the next closest quarterback is Josh Allen at 28.39. He’s also completing north of 72 percent of his passes, which ranks fourth among quarterbacks with at least 25 dropbacks, and his nine touchdown passes are tied with Kirk Cousins for the league lead.

Additionally, we can throw away the narrative that Purdy is solely producing due to being in Kyle Shanahan’s system because when the play has gone off script, Purdy has remained terrific. He ranks third in EPA per play when pressured, and his three touchdown passes under pressure are second in the league. And because of Purdy’s strong play to begin the season, the 49ers are 3-0. I can admit when I’m wrong, and I was wrong from the very beginning about Purdy – what a player he has blossomed into over the last handful of seasons.

Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy put on vintage performance

After a Week 2 loss that truly felt like an early rock bottom for the Pittsburgh Steelers’ offense, Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy turned the hourglass upside down and delivered the explosive offense that Steelers fans were promised upon McCarthy’s hiring back in January. After scoring just 16 points in the first two games, the Steelers’ offensive unit exploded for 30 points against a Cincinnati Bengals defense that entered Week 3 coming off a dominant showing against the Houston Texans in which they didn’t allow a touchdown. Rodgers threw three touchdown passes, running back Jaylen Warren racked up 127 yards on the ground, and the Steelers totaled 411 yards en route to defeating their division rivals to get to 2-1. Even in a new era, it is dangerous to count out the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Case Keenum, Ben Johnson lift Bears over Eagles

Performances like the one we saw from Case Keenum to close Week 3 are why we love sports. After injuries to both Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent, the 38 year-old Keenum was thrust into the starting lineup in what would be his first regular season game in north of 1,000 days. You wouldn’t have known it had been that long since the University of Houston legend suited up, though, by how well he played. On his first drive, he drove the Bears down the field and threw a touchdown to Luther Burden. And with a 13-7 lead in the third quarter, Keenum connected with Kalif Raymond for a 41-yard touchdown pass that ended up being the nail in the coffin for the Philadelphia Eagles.

Keenum finished the game going 24-of-34 for 247 yards and three total touchdowns, as Ben Johnson put together a masterpiece of play-calling against a Vic Fangio defense while holding the Eagles to their fewest points in a game during the Nick Sirianni era.

One play that changed everything

The ending of the back-and-forth shootout between the Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys featured several questionable decisions, but the one that may be getting overshadowed is the kickoff from Dallas to Baltimore at the end of regulation. After Dak Prescott purposely air-mailed a ball out of bounds despite having George Pickens open in the front of the end zone for the potential go-ahead touchdown, the Cowboys kicked the game-tying field goal and kicked the ball back to the Ravens with just seven seconds remaining. However, instead of putting the ball in play, Brandon Aubrey booted a touchback, which didn’t take any time off the clock. That would have been forgiven if the Cowboys just played the normal prevent zone we see in these situations. Instead, they played man defense, which allowed Lamar Jackson to connect with Zay Flowers, call a timeout, and bring out Tyler Loop for the game-winning field goal. Should the Cowboys miss out on the postseason, this will be a game they look back on and wonder how they did so much so wrong in such a short sequence of plays.

Buy or sell

Buy: Jacksonville Jaguars

The Jaguars are 2-1, and both of their wins have come in blowout fashion. After a 35-6 dismantling of the defending AFC Champion New England Patriots, the Jaguars sit comfortably atop the AFC South, and their quarterback is off to a fantastic start. Trevor Lawrence is ninth in the league in EPA per play (min. 25 dropbacks) and his seven touchdown passes rank third in the league. Throw in the fact that the Jaguars are also fourth in defensive EPA per play, and you have a team that looks bound to repeat their success from 2025.

Sell: Denver Broncos

It’s infuriating watching the Broncos. I can see with my eyes that Bo Nix isn’t good, and yet somehow their defense will come alive and make enough plays to put their offense in the perfect position to score just enough points to win. And while that’s all well and good, this isn’t sustainable. Especially when Bo Nix has a lower EPA per play than Cam Ward. I’ll end up being right. For the time being, though, Broncos fans will continue to convince themselves they can win the Super Bowl.

Buy: Texans, Bucs, Chargers are done

All three of these teams had playoff expectations entering the 2026 season. And as it pertains to the Texans and Chargers, some were each of them to be the AFC representative in the Super Bowl.

We can talk about how great the Texans’ defense is all we want – it doesn’t matter when the offense can’t score points, which is exactly what we said would be the only thing that could keep the Texans from reaching their potential. They’ve allowed just 39 points over the last two weeks, but their offense scored 23 points. Yes, they overcame this exact deficit last season, but to expect that type of turnaround in consecutive years would be a big ask.

The Chargers were our cover story last week, and so I ask once again – what is the excuse for Justin Herbert this week? Go on, Herbert hive. Tell me how it isn’t his fault that he only put up 16 points after his defense forced five turnovers. Tell me how he isn’t to blame for squandering a fumble recovery in plus territory by throwing a terrible interception right back to the Bills. Josh Allen certainly didn’t play a good game himself, but the difference between good quarterbacks and elite quarterbacks is overcoming poor performances and still finding ways to win. Allen did that. Patrick Mahomes did that. When has Herbert done that? The Chargers also have the hardest remaining schedule in the league – they’re done.

Throw in Baker Mayfield’s thumb injury keeping him out for 2-4 weeks and Tampa having to turn to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels and you have a trio of teams whose season is all but over before we even reached October.

Sell: Drake Maye

It pains me to say it, but yeah. Something is clearly wrong, and it’s not new to 2026. Maye hasn’t played a quality game since Week 17 against the Jets in 2025. He currently has one touchdown pass to six interceptions, and his decision-making has been questionable at best and unacceptable at worst. Have we ever seen this abrupt of a drop-off from a quarterback where he goes from being MVP runner-up to a legitimate net negative for his team? This feels like an unfortunate first of its kind case study.

Prediction to track

  • Week 1: Steelers will trade Joey Porter Jr: TBD
  • Week 2: Rams will beat Broncos handedly: Incorrect

Well, the Rams ruined what was set to be a spot-on prediction, so now we conclude Week 3 hoping to get on the board with our predictions. With that in mind, I’ll go back to the primetime blowout well and say the Sunday Night Football matchup between the Lions and Panthers will be a decisive win for Detroit. Carolina was a team that got far too overrated heading into the season after winning eight games in 2025. My one concern is that Bryce Young has taken advantage of bad secondaries thus far, and the Lions do have a bad secondary so I’m really setting myself up for failure. That said, Detroit’s offense is too good to not have one of their yearly routs where they drop 40+ points. Even if the Panthers do connect on some explosive touchdowns, Detroit wins 41-24.

item.title: Green Bay Packers News: Brian Gutekunst makes an attempt to fix offensive line
item.description: Better than nothing, I guess?
item.content:encoded:
Offensive line? Yeah, consider that fixed.

The Packers have signed not one (Cordell Volson), not two (Laken Tomlinson), but three (Mekhi Becton) linemen that nobody else wanted to put on their 53-man roster. Checkmate, everybody else. Contender status has been restored in Green Bay.

Color me underwhelmed by the Packers’ sudden urgent desire to fix their offensive line. Though Brian Gutekunst has seemingly answered fans’ pleas to add to the offensive line, we should have healthy skepticism about any lineman available in late September. The last few seasons of NFL football have shown the world the value of a good offensive line (and the Packers have shown what can happen with a bad one, for that matter), and I don’t think anybody’s just letting good prospects sit at home on their couch when they play a position as important as we understand the line to be.

Still, at least they’re doing something, right? The Packers’ trio of offensive line acquisitions are all former starters. Not all of their previous work is good, mind you, and Tomlinson in particular is well into the “journeyman” phase of his career, though he was once a Pro Bowl caliber player. They may be limited now, but each of them has a more impressive resume than anyone the Packers have put on the field at guard to this point. Even if Tomlinson’s Pro Bowl came when Donovan Jennings still had two seasons of college ball to go, he’s a far sight more accomplished than his younger counterpart.

It boils down to this: at least they’re doing something. Is it too little too late? Quite possibly, even probably. But at least it’s something, and if it makes the Packers more watchable for the rest of the season, they’ll have accomplished something.

Packers working on offensive line from different angles | Packers.com

I like this approach much better than the “don’t work on the offensive line at all” idea they went with for the first three weeks.

Can Mekhi Becton and other veterans signings save Packers offensive line? | Packers Wire

Even if the answer here is “probably not,” trying something is better than not trying anything.

Matt LaFleur believes Packers offense needs to deliver more ‘body blows’ | Packers News ($)

If the Packers can figure out a way to grind out a few yards on the ground, it could open things up for the rest of the offense.

Packers-Buccaneers Matchups: Both Teams Have Huge Advantages | Sports Illustrated

I don’t want to hear about any advantages the Buccaneers have. 

How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list | ESPN

This article makes a big deal about how Myles Garrett has averaged 14 sacks a year for the last five seasons, but it doesn’t really focus much on how he’d have to keep up that pace for more than five more seasons to break the all-time sack record, and he’d be 37 by the time he does it.

item.title: Why didn’t George Kittle take a knee? Kyle Shanahan didn’t tell him to
item.description: George Kittle could have kneeled. Instead he scored Kyle Shanahan forgot to tell him not to.
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco 49ers beat the Arizona Cardinals Sunday 36-30 and as the Cardinals went to their onside kick in an attempt to win the game, one question entered my mind:

What was George Kittle doing running that final touchdown into the end zone?

The touchdown is nice. Especially when Brock Purdy scored one two downs earlier with a near 50-yard scramble. Unfortunately that touchdown got nullified thanks to a holding call on none other than Kittle. Had Kittle taken a knee, the anxiety of the game possibly getting snatched from the 49ers would be nothing. The Cardinals had no timeouts, and the clock was well below the two-minute warning. A knee on the 1-yard line and the 49ers can run the clock out leading to the game ending 29-27, 49ers. Instead, we got this:

Now look, no one is disputing the awesomeness of the touchdown itself, especially with the background behind it. That said, why not take a knee? Kittle had just the perfect opening to even go out of bounds. Stops the clock, but at least the 49ers can still tick the thing down, and the Cardinals can never take the field again.

Kittle was just doing what he normally does.

“Probably should have gone out of bounds,” Kittle told reporters after the game. “We could have just kneeled it out. But no one told me to, so that’s their fault, not mine.”

The 49ers head coach shouldered responsibility for not delivering the memo:

“That was on me,” Kyle Shanahan said. “I didn’t remind him in the huddle and I don’t expect him to be paying attention to the clock. But I definitely wish I did.”

What resulted was the Cardinals trying to move down the field with a minute and change and electing to kick a 49-yard field goal on 2nd and 10 with 34 seconds left. 34 seconds is a sliver of time to get the obvious onside kick and then try to get it in the endzone proper. The plan didn’t work as the kicked ball rolled into the waiting arms of a Deebo Samuel.

Leave it to George Kittle—or is it Kyle Shanahan—to leave us glued to the monitor until the very, very end.

item.title: Klint Kubiak is the early favorite for coach of the year
item.description: In the battle of the offensive coordinators of the last two Super Bowl winners, Raiders coach Klint Kubiak got the better of Saints coach Kellen Moore.
item.content:encoded:
In the battle of the offensive coordinators of the last two Super Bowl winners, Raiders coach Klint Kubiak got the better of Saints coach Kellen Moore.

The 35-27 victory moved the Raiders to 3-0. To no surprise, Kubiak is the early favorite for coach of the year.

One big reason for that is "coach of the year" typically means "coach whose team most exceeded the generally accepted preseason expectations." Under that test, it could be no one (for now) other than Kubiak.

The Raiders were 3-14 in 2025. They're now 3-0. And they've played well enough to show it's not a fluke.

Meanwhile, Kubiak has become only the third Raiders coach to launch his career with three straight wins. The others were Bill Callahan in 2002 and John Madden in 1969.

Callahan took the Raiders to the Super Bowl. Madden, in his first year, took the Raiders to the AFL Championship. If Kubiak simply takes the Raiders to the 7th seed, he'll likely be getting a trophy that his father, Gary, never won. While pursuing the possibility of having the first father-son picnic that consists of both guys showing up with a Super Bowl trophy.

item.title: Houston Texans Opening Odds vs Dallas Cowboys

item.content:encoded:
The Texas-sized showdown of the Houston Texans (0-3) against the Dallas Cowboys (1-2) is more exciting on paper than in reality. These two teams have struggled out of the gate and are desperate to turn their seasons around in Week 4.

FanDuel has you covered whether you’re from Texas or just looking for some additional action this weekend. Below are the Spread, Moneyline, and Over/Under heading into the game against Dallas.

The Spread: Texans -2.5

Considering the Texans are 0-3 and haven’t looked competent on offense since the first half of the first game of the season, this is an astonishing line. I cannot imagine Reliant Stadium will be rocking. If anything, this could be a stadium quick to turn on the team if they fall behind. The Cowboys, though 1-2 entering the contest, have scored 20, 37, and 31 points. Houston hasn’t proved it can move the ball against even the weakest of defenses, as seen against the Colts, which doesn’t bode well against a high-powered offense.

Until the Texans win a game, take the opponent and the extra points for insurance.

Moneyline: Texans -136

The Texans are 3-4 all time against the Cowboys. Given their recent struggles and lack of anything expected to change, It’s hard to believe the Texans can steal a win against the Cowboys.

What will be interesting to watch is if the defense can keep a lid on the Cowboys passing attack. Derek Stingley Jr. and Kamari Lassiter have not impressed and are concerning when paired up against CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. At this juncture in the seasons, it’s difficult to believe the Texans will outright beat an opponent. Wait till they are, hopefully, on a role before taking them straight up.

Over/Under: 47.5

The Texans went well under last week’s line of 44.5 against the Colts as well as the 45.5 mark against the Bengals, but managed to blow out the Over/Under against the Bills in a high-scoring matchup. This Over/Under is a tad elevated compared to the two previous lines, most likely due to the high-octane offense in Dallas. That said, Houston’s current offensive form doesn’t bode well to betting the over. If Nico Collins is back in the lineup, then the over is something to consider. Collins’ presence unlocks the passing game and lessens the pressure on the run.

The Cowboys defense have allowed a bevy of points thus far. They’ve given up 28, 20, and 34 points in their three matchups. Given how porous their defense has been AND if Nico Collins is set to go Sunday, then take the Over in a competitive and integral matchup between two teams vying to keep their seasons alive early in the 2026 campaign.

item.title: Bears' T.J. Edwards nabbed clutch INT vs Eagles. Did he steal the play call?
item.description: Bears linebacker T.J. Edwards appeared to be sneakily listening in to the Eagles' calls at the line of scrimmage before intercepting Jalen Hurts.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Bears linebacker T.J. Edwards got creative in his efforts to gain an upper hand in his team's Week 3 "Monday Night Football" matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Late in the third quarter, Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was attempting to change a play at the line of the scrimmage when Edwards aligned himself just over the center. The 30-year-old linebacker appeared to be trying to listen to what Hurts was saying ahead of the play.

Edwards was able to drop back into coverage on the play and intercept Hurts. That led many to wonder whether the veteran, who played for the Eagles from 2019 and 2022, had heard something familiar at the line that allowed him to position himself for the interception.
