item.title: Boss Hog of the Week: Sonny Styles, Marcus Mariota among best Commanders from Week 3
item.description: There are several options for the Boss Hog of the Week after the Commanders’ victory over the Seahawks. Vote now!
item.content:encoded:
Every victory deserves some serious love in this league, and the players who deliver standout performances deserve to be recognized. After two disheartening weeks, our squad bounced back with a massive, hard-fought 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday at Northwest Stadium.  

To celebrate, I wanted to create a space for us fans to give credit where credit is due and honor the guys who truly stepped up when we needed it most. 

This introduces our new weekly tradition: The Boss Hog of the Week. Moving forward, I hope to keep these fan votes running throughout the entire season. The rules are simple: each week represents a standalone vote, and at the end of the year, I’ll tally up all the weekly winners to crown the official, definitive Boss Hog of the season. 

Without further ado, let’s look at the standout performers. Here are your nominees for this week’s award: 

QB Marcus Mariota  

Stat line: 19-for-31, 183 passing yards, 3 passing TDs, 0 INTs | 5 carries, 11 rushing yards 

Marcus Mariota stepped into a high-pressure situation and delivered exactly what this team needed. Following a deflating loss to Dallas, Mariota was named the starter for the week with Jayden Daniels sidelined with a left elbow dislocation. In a massive show of confidence, the team also named him an all-season captain — and he rewarded that trust. 

Mariota led a smart, calculated attack, exploiting a Seattle defense that was missing both starting safeties. While it wasn’t always pretty, it was efficient, largely mistake-free football. He finished the day throwing for three touchdowns and sealed the victory himself, picking up a critical first down on a gritty third-and-7 run to run out the clock. It was a remarkably strong, poised performance from the veteran, who will now look to carry this momentum across the pond as the team heads to London. 

WR Terry McLaurin 

Stat line: 5 receptions, 78 receiving Yards, 1 receiving TD 

Terry McLaurin stepped up when his team needed him most. After frustratingly missing out on the end zone three separate times last week, McLaurin bounced back with a rock-solid performance to finally find paydirt this week. While he didn’t quite match the explosive stat line put up by his opponent, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, his impact on the outcome of the game was undeniable. McLaurin’s clutch 30-yard touchdown reception gave the team the necessary cushion to maintain the lead, serving as a perfect example of a squad that simply refused to give up. It was exactly the kind of gritty, winning football you want to see from a true leader. 

LB Sonny Styles

Stat line: 4 solo tackles, 1 assisted tackle, 1 interception, 2 passes defensed, 1 forced fumble, 1 QB Hit. 

Sonny Styles had a true breakout performance. Many fans, including myself, thought his transition to this important defensive role would be a steep hill to climb, but he is completely shattering those expectations. He has been progressing week-to-week, proving that, while there are still areas to refine, he is absolutely fearless when facing a challenge. 

He was an absolute menace and an instant playmaker on Sunday, single-handedly disrupting the offense by being a part of two massive turnovers. His most impressive sequence didn’t even show up on the turnover sheet. It was a jaw-dropping play where he went stride-for-stride down the field with explosive Seattle running back Jadarian Price, perfectly tracking the ball to force a clutch pass breakup. That rare combination of size, speed, and coverage ability is exactly what Washington’s defense was desperately missing all of last season. He isn’t just surviving the transition; he’s becoming a star in the process. 

CB Amik Robertson

Stat line: 6 total tackles (4 Solo), 4 passes defensed, 1 forced fumble 

The box score won’t reveal Amik Robertson’s true impact. Not just on Sunday, but over the previous weeks. 

Amik has been head-and-shoulders above the rest as the best cornerback on this team. He has fought tooth-and-nail to make every play miserable and difficult for opposing wide receivers. He was targeted relentlessly on Sunday, ultimately allowing four receptions for 36 yards and a touchdown, all to Seattle’s elite wideout Smith-Njigba. 

What truly earned Amik a spot on this ballot is his sheer, unyielding effort. Whether it’s laying out for pass breakups, ripping the ball away for a forced fumble or great pursuit to ensure a play doesn’t extend an inch further, he refuses to give up. Amik has established himself as the heart and soul of this defensive backfield, a secondary that should get better when Trey Amos makes his return. 

LB Kain Medrano  

The Stat Line: 5 Total Tackles (3 Solo), 1 Interception, 1 Pass Defended, 1 QB Hit, 1 Touchdown (Pick-Six). 

Welcome to the show, Kain! I had some very strong reservations about Medrano. He still has some clear tackling issues that carried over from his college days, but stepping into the fire the moment Leo Chenal went down was the ultimate test. He didn’t just fill a gap; he made arguably the play of the game with that beautiful interception on Sam Darnold, taking it to the house for a spectacular touchdown. It was an absolutely incredible moment for a player who simply kept his head down, stayed ready, and answered the call the second his chance arrived. 

OC David Blough 

David Blough deserves tons of love for this win, too. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald’s defense has been an absolute buzzsaw since last season. That background makes this masterpiece of a game even more impressive for our first-year play caller. Blough drew up an excellent game plan and executed it beautifully. Seattle hadn’t given up an explosive play all year until Blough dialed up that 21-yard screen play to receiver Jaylin Lane. Following that up with the 30-yard touchdown strike to Terry McLaurin made it two explosive cracks. Even with several key players missing from his own unit, Blough kept a top defense completely off-balance and confused at times. This was a statement game for Blough, and doing it against a defensive juggernaut is a huge bonus for our coaching staff moving forward. 

This is the type of game that will either be a once-in-a-blue-moon moment or the exact shift of energy the Commanders needed to bounce back for the rest of the season. But, for right now, let’s just enjoy this massive upset! 

Be sure to vote in the poll below, and if there’s anyone I missed, make sure to post them in the comments. I hope you all enjoy this new series!

item.title: Case Keenum went from forgotten QB to Bears hero on Monday Night Football
item.description: Case Keenum turned back the clock at 38 years old to save the Bears in a stunning win over the Eagles.
item.content:encoded:
Case Keenum took the field as the starting quarterback for the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football against the Philadelphia Eagles for his first regular-season action since the 2023 NFL season.

And the veteran turned back the clock, guiding the Bears to a surprising 27-7 victory.

To put Keenum’s football journey in perspective, the 38-year-old quarterback was a member of the 2006 high school recruiting class, along with players such as Percy Harvin, Sergio Kindle, Myron Rolle, Tim Tebow, DeMarco Murray, Gerald McCoy, LeSean McCoy, and Brandon Graham.

Yet, there Keenum was on Monday Night Football, leading the Bears to a most unexpected victory as the team’s starting quarterback, in the wake of injuries to starter Caleb Williams and backup Tyson Bagent.

“Playing well anytime in your career feels good,” Keenum said after a performance that earned him a game ball from head coach Ben Johnson. “To do it on ‘Monday Night Football’ after you thought you weren’t ever going to play again multiple times. Golly, this is special. It’s really special. And I don’t know if I’ll be able to put it into words tonight, but I’m going to enjoy it tonight, that’s for sure.”

Keenum completed 24-of-34 passes for 247 yards and a pair of touchdowns on a night where everyone, including Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, expected the Bears to run the football as much as possible to help their third-string quarterback. While the Bears struggled to get the running game going until late, and Johnson even spoke about the need to run the football during a halftime interview with ESPN, Keenum kept slinging it.

And slinging it well.

His first touchdown pass, an underneath shovel pass to Luther Burden, came as a result of an incredible individual effort from the wide receiver and his teammates, as he bullied his way into the end zone after being initially stopped well short of the goal line.

Keenum’s second touchdown pass, however, had a higher level of difficulty:

Motion at the snap from Burden creates some confusion in the secondary, as both Cooper DeJean and Tariq Woolen end up over Burden on the outside. That frees up Kalif Raymond on a post route, and Keenum punishes the mistake, snapping off a quick throw to Raymond, who does the rest.

But it is clear from the gameplan that Johnson had every bit of trust in Keenum. Early in the first quarter the Bears faced a 4th-and-1 at the Philadelphia 32-yard line, and not only did Johnson keep his offense on the field, but he put the ball in Keenum’s hands for this throw to the flat:

This is quick thinking from the quarterback.

Keenum also punished the blitz, when Fangio decided to bring pressure. According to charting data the Eagles blitzed Keenum on 12 dropbacks last night.

On those snaps, the third-string quarterback completed 11-of-11 passes for 145 yards, and both touchdowns. His best throw of the night, from my perspective, came against the blitz, this deep out route to Rome Odunze in the face of heavy pressure late in the second quarter:

Keenum’s performance, particularly against the blitz, might just have been born out of his preparation leading up to Monday night. With both Williams and Bagent sidelined — Williams due to a hamstring issue and Bagent in the concussion protocol — Keenum was running the show for Chicago this week. He was the only quarterback to practice all three days last week as he prepared for the Eagles.

That spilled over to the quarterback meeting on Sunday night, as Johnson told ESPN:

“It was the night before the game. We always do our quarterback meeting,” Johnson said after the game. “He ran the show, and the coaching staff kind of took a back seat. There were no reminders from us. He was just going through the list of every single play that was on the plan, and what he was going to do, and gave us his favorites. And that was really — I thought that right there is a good indicator of what it’s going to look like on game day.”

Johnson also spoke about Keenum’s awareness after the win:

“He knows where everyone is supposed to be on every single play and so he is really quick to recognize coverage,” said the head coach. “He knows why we’re calling the play and what we’re looking for and if we’re not getting that he’s accelerating through it really quickly. That’s what you get when you’re 15-plus years playing that position in this league.”

As for the quarterback, he called the chance at another “shot” to play in the NFL something “you dream of” as a player:

“To get a shot again like this? Yeah, you dream of it,” Keenum said. “That’s why I’m still here doing this when I get knocked down. I got knocked down my whole career. I just keep getting up, coming to work, just keep bouncing back.”

And with Williams expected to be sidelined longer, and after his performance on Monday night, he could get another shot or two this season.

But even if he does not get another shot, it was one incredible night for the quarterback. And adding to the experience, it was the first time Keenum’s two young children were able to see him play in person:

“Hopefully they stayed up. Hopefully they didn’t fall asleep over there. We kept it exciting for them,” said Keenum. “I’m going to have fun watching the game with them tomorrow on the couch, or probably just Bluey. They probably won’t want to watch it again. They’ll be like, ‘We saw it one time already, dad.’ 

There is also one other note about that 2006 recruiting class, beyond Keenum.

Another member of that group?

Matthew Stafford.

Give it up for the old guys.

item.title: Titans QB Cam Ward is wasting this offensive line
item.description: Tennessee Titans QB Cam Ward is ruining improvement from this offensive line after the Week 3 loss.
item.content:encoded:
Remember when everyone was worried about the Tennessee Titans’ offensive line prior to the 2026 season starting? Fast forward past Week 3 and the tape has revealed an even more concerning revelation. Sophomore quarterback Cam Ward is actually wasting a pretty good offensive line.

Pro Football Focus has the Titans’ pass-protection unit ranked as No. 3 in the entire NFL, with a grade of 71.9. Through three weeks, Titans left tackle Dan Moore Jr. is the team’s only offensive lineman who has been assigned primary blame for a sack. Ward has been sacked on just five occasions through three games.

Collectively, the Titans’ starting five has allowed 16 pressures. Some of these numbers may be slightly too favorable, but the point gets across. The Titans have done an excellent job protecting Ward in the passing game.

ESPN Analytics has the Titans as a middling unit in pass protection. Whichever metric you believe, the takeaway is similar. The Titans have fielded a pretty good offensive line in protection. Ward is wasting that effort away.

Ward has bailed some clean pockets. Inaccurate misses have been a weekly occurrence. The situation reached a boiling point on Sunday when Ward left 14 points on the board through two glaring red-zone errors in Week 3.

As a rookie, many of the offense’s shortcomings were blamed on Ward’s supporting cast. That’s no longer the case. The offensive line has been upgraded. The wide receiver corps looks way better with Wan’Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate.

The unfortunate truth is that Ward is the biggest preventative factor from the offense showing improvement right now. He’s a young QB who is struggling mightily in a new system, but many of his struggles are issues that date back to his rookie season (bad footwork, inaccurate passes).

Ward needs to start playing better before the Titans consider doing something rash in 2027.

item.title: Bears vs. Eagles: Inside the Snap Counts, Stats, and a Sucker Sneak
item.description: Here are the Bears' snap counts, individual stats, and a few team stats from the Bears' huge 27-7 win over the Eagles from @wiltfongjr.
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, that rainy game last week was the anomaly, because with a 27 to 7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles, the Chicago Bears are who we thought they were.

While many expected (including me) the Bears to dust off an old-school ground-and-pound game plan to protect 38-year-old Case Keenum, Chicago went the other direction and aired it out. They called more pass plays than run plays and showed complete trust in their third-string quarterback.

Ben Johnson’s offensive game plan last night was brilliant. A season ago, he ran all over this talented Eagles front, but this time, it was the quick passing game that diced up Vic Fangio’s Philadelphia defense, and that caught the Eagles off guard.

The Bears had more total yards (375 to 248), more first downs (24 to 14), and had the time-of-possession edge (36:53 to 23:07). That 23:07 is the Eagles’ second-lowest time of possession in their last 42 games, worse than only last year’s Black Friday game against the Bears (20:42).

Let’s look at the Bears’ playing time breakdowns and a few individual stats from the game.

OFFENSE

Case Keenum is now 4-0 when playing against a Vic Fangio-coordinated defense.

Keenum was a perfect 10 for 10 when the Eagles blitzed him for 140 yards, a +1.18 EPA/dropback, and a 90% success rate.

Keenum now holds the record for the oldest player to score a rushing touchdown in Bears history, and he did it on a play designed by a former Bears’ offensive coordinator.

“That’s a Mike Martz special right there,” Ben Johnson said about the TD. “That’s the old sucker sneak, and I think that they were a little bit tight initially, and then they stemmed out at the last second, which gave us the green light to get to that play, and, you know, it’s an old play but a good play right there.”

DEFENSE

I was told all offseason that there would be a turnover regression, but Chicago’s defense had three more takeaways, including safety Dillon Thieneman’s first career interception. Again, last week was the anomaly, because in Week 1 they also had three takeaways.

Austin Booker had a Peanut Punch, and Dayo Odeyingbo had a sack! T.J. Edwards had a pick and a career-high 3 passes defended.

Dennis Allen’s defense has now stacked two good games in a row after getting lit up Week 1. They held the Eagles to 2 for 9 on third-down attempts (22.2%) and stopped Philly on both of their fourth-down tries.

SPECIAL TEAMS*

*The above image has players who only played in the third phase.

Cairo Santos hit all three extra points and both field goals, but he missed the landing zone on another kickoff, resulting in a penalty. You have to assume he’s being coached to try and dirty kick these short to mess up the timing of the returns, but he needs to get this right.

Tory Taylor had 2 punts for a 52.5 average (38.5 net) with 1 inside the 20. He nearly had a second down near the goal line, but a rookie mistake by Sam Roush turned it into a touchback.

Zavion Thomas had a 32-yard kickoff return.

Elijah Hicks had 2 special teams tackles.

New (old) long snapper Scott Daly was perfect on all his snaps.

To check out the complete Bears vs. Eagles box score, I find ESPN’s site is easy to navigate.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan explains why he was impressed with 49ers’ depleted D-Line in Week 3
item.description: The 49ers had only 10 pressures
item.content:encoded:
It’s no secret that the 49ers are extremely thin on the defensive line, and the pressure numbers from their Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals reflect that.

Per Pro Football Focus, the 49ers managed only 12 pressures of Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett, getting home on two as Ogbo Okoronkwo and Keion White recorded sacks.

It was always likely to be tough sledding for the 49ers’ front from a pass-rushing perspective without Nick Bosa and rookie Romello Height, and with impressive rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton leaving the game with cramps in the second half.

But, speaking in his Monday conference call, head coach Kyle Shanahan explained why he was more than satisfied with the performance of the Niners’ young and depleted D-Line.

Said Shanahan:

“By no means was it perfect, but I was real proud of how they played. They really competed their asses off. They were running to the ball, working real hard. I thought they did a good job throughout the game. I think they all kind of died out a little bit as the game went, just getting those plays up into the 80s and then losing Gracen to the cramps and stuff, which just took the numbers down some. But, we were able to change up our fronts throughout the game. We asked a lot of them and considering the circumstances for them, I thought it was a real successful game for them.”

With Raheem Morris as the defensive coordinator, the 49ers have become more multiple up front. Morris frequently mixes in five-man fronts, and he presented the Cardinals with several different looks last Sunday, with his deployment of Fred Warner as an extra rusher proving successful in speeding up Brissett’s clock.

While playing in a variety of different fronts, Osa Odighizuwa (82%), White (69%), Khalid Kareem (62%) and Okoronkwo (55%) all featured on over 50 percent of the defensive snaps.

That is a huge mental and physical strain to put on a thin group and, in those circumstances, a return of two sacks and only 90 yards surrendered Jeremiyah Love on the ground represents a solid day from the 49er D-Line.

It is not an effort Shanahan will want that group to have to put in regularly, and help is on the way with Height returning to practice following surgery on his broken hand, Matthew Judon being signed to the practice squad and Mykel Williams seeing his practice window opened after starting the year on the PUP list.

Reinforcements are on the way ahead of more exacting challenges for the 49ers against the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks in the next two weeks. However, those who held the fort on the defensive side of the trenches against Arizona can afford to hold their heads high.
